title: Over the Fairgrounds
subtitle: A drone over the Harwick Fairgrounds crowd on a NO FLY day

brief.userPrompt: A 6,000-person public event is under way at the Harwick Fairgrounds beside Horton Field on a NO FLY day: the flight operations desk logged all twelve aircraft in Hangar 1 at 0800. Harwick Police's contracted detection vendor shows a drone with a Remote ID track circling over the crowd, and a bystander post with a photo blames the Group because its hangar is next door. The Group must prove from the schedule and the fleet register that every aircraft is grounded, lend an RPIC to the Harwick Police command post to interpret Remote ID data if asked, never launch, interfere with or chase the aircraft, coordinate with Harwick Police, CCSO and the FAA, and answer the post through Corporate Communications only.
constraints: Every email address of the Group and its units uses the exercise domain huog.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 10, the Harwick Daily News); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (Harwick Police, its detection vendor, CCSO, the FAA, event organizers, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Proving a negative fast, helping the police without touching another aircraft, and telling the truth when the operator turns out to be one of your own people
overview.threat: On Saturday, September 19, the Harwick Fall Festival draws about 6,000 people to the Harwick Fairgrounds beside Horton Field. It is a NO FLY day for the Group: the flight operations desk logged all twelve aircraft in Hangar 1 at 0800. Shortly after 11:00 Harwick Police’s contracted detection vendor shows a small quadcopter broadcasting Remote ID and circling over the crowd at about 240 ft. Its operator position sits in the north lot by the Group’s fence, a bystander post blames “the drone company next door”, and the aircraft looks like the Group’s own small quadcopters.
overview.operationalImpact: The Group has no counter-UAS capability and must not launch, chase, jam or interfere with the aircraft (HUOG-ERP 8.4). Its job is to prove within five minutes from the schedule and the fleet register that every Group aircraft is grounded, lend an RPIC to Harwick Police’s command post if asked to read the Remote ID data, and say only true things through Corporate Communications. The incident turns when police find the operator: a part-time visual observer of the Group flying his personal drone on his day off. The Group then has to decide what to say publicly, what to tell the FAA and its clients, and what to do about the crew member, without letting “no Group aircraft were flying” become a misleading answer.

overview.targetAudience: Flight Operations, Aviation Safety, Leadership, Corporate Communications, Security / Harwick Police liaison
overview.location: Millbrook Road hangar complex and Horton Field, beside the Harwick Fairgrounds, Harwick, Calder County, New York

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Answer Harwick Police within five minutes from the schedule and the fleet register, and keep Flight Operations, Aviation Safety, Leadership, the police liaison and Corporate Communications on one set of facts.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Decide what the Group says publicly once its own crew member is identified as the operator, and how the Group handles him, without misleading statements (decision point).

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Help Harwick Police interpret the Remote ID data and compare it with the fleet register, without launching, tracking with Group aircraft or interfering with the drone (HUOG-ERP 8.4).

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Follow HUOG-ERP 8.4 and HUOG-FOM 7.6, the Section 6 notifications (Harwick Police, the FSDO, Corporate Communications) and the UC-CP-2025 rule that only Corporate Communications speaks to the media.

roles.name: Director of Flight Operations (Flight Operations)
roles.description: Owns the flight schedule, the fleet register and crew rosters; Incident Commander when aircraft are involved; answers whether any Group aircraft is airborne.
standingOrders: Answer Harwick Police within five minutes from the schedule and the fleet register (HUOG-ERP 8.4).
No Group aircraft launches to look for, follow or identify another drone.
Lend an RPIC to the police command post only to read Remote ID data.
Record every call and decision in the incident log.

roles.name: General Manager (Leadership)
roles.description: Accountable executive and spokesperson with Corporate Communications; joins the Harwick Police call when a reported drone is suspected to be a Group aircraft; decides on client and regulator notification.
standingOrders: Join the Harwick Police call when the drone is suspected to be a Group aircraft (HUOG-ERP 8.4).
Only the General Manager may ask Harwick Police for an exception to a NO FLY day.
Decide what clients and the public are told, with facts.
Personnel decisions follow the facts and the FSDO’s view, not the headlines.

roles.name: Aviation Safety Officer (Aviation Safety)
roles.description: Owns the safety case, regulator reporting and the event record; the Group’s contact with the FSDO.
standingOrders: Preserve every record: the 0800 fleet count, the register extract, Remote ID data and photographs.
Report to the FSDO what the Group knows, the same day.
Interfering with an aircraft is a federal offense, whoever flies it.
Recommend crew actions from facts, not from the press.

roles.name: Corporate Communications (Communications)
roles.description: Owns all external messaging under UC-CP-2025; the Group never speaks to the media directly.
standingOrders: Only Corporate Communications speaks to the media; crews and staff refer every question.
Say only what is true and complete enough not to mislead.
Coordinate with the Harwick Police PIO before naming anyone.
Give a time for the next update every time.

roles.name: Fleet & Logistics Manager (Security / Harwick Police liaison)
roles.description: Owns Hangar 1 and the physical security of the hangars, keys and the perimeter road; liaison to Harwick Police and CCSO.
standingOrders: Count and photograph the aircraft and batteries in Hangar 1 when asked to prove the fleet is grounded.
Keep the Group’s people away from the drone, the operator and any evidence; that is police work.
Pass every police request to the Incident Commander and log it.
Know who has access to the perimeter road and the hangar keys.

phases.title: Is It Ours?
phases.goal: Prove within minutes that every Group aircraft is grounded and give Harwick Police what it needs, while the crowd and the internet blame the Group.
beats: At 11:05 Harwick Police’s detection console shows a Remote ID drone circling the crowd; police ask whether any Group aircraft is airborne.
At 11:10 the flight operations desk confirms the 0800 count from the register; at 11:15 police ask for an RPIC at the command post.
At 11:30 the console photo shows a quadcopter that looks like the Group’s small aircraft, with a serial not on the register.
At 11:40 the fair organizer demands the Group “get its drone down”; at 11:50 a bystander post blames the Group.

phases.title: The Operator by the Fence
phases.goal: Support the police command post with Remote ID expertise as the drone returns and its operator position moves next to the Group’s fence.
beats: At 12:05 the drone is back and its operator position is on the perimeter road beside Hangar 1.
At 12:10 Channel 10 has video it says shows a launch from behind the hangar.
At 12:15 Hangar 1 is counted and photographed; at 12:25 the police sergeant asks who can use the perimeter road.

phases.title: One of Ours
phases.goal: Decide what to say, and what to do, when the operator turns out to be a Group crew member flying his own drone.
beats: At 13:05 police stop the operator in the north lot: he says he is one of the Group’s part-time visual observers.
At 13:10 the FSDO asks whether the flight was a Group operation; at 13:15 the Harwick Police PIO is about to issue a statement — the decision point.
At 13:20 Flight Operations finds him on Monday’s CP&L roster; at 13:25 the post spreads.

phases.title: Telling It Straight
phases.goal: Close the day with accurate records, an FSDO report, a client answer and a public statement that does not mislead.
beats: At 14:05 police keep the drone and controller as evidence and ask for the Group’s records.
At 14:15 CP&L asks whether Monday’s inspection is still on; at 14:20 the Harwick Daily News asks about the Group’s policy on personal flights.
At 14:25 the ASO drafts the event record and the FSDO follow-up.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 11:00 on Saturday, September 19. The Harwick Fall Festival is under way next door with about 6,000 people. Today is a NO FLY day for the Group: at 0800 the flight operations desk logged all twelve aircraft in Hangar 1. The weather is clear, 68°F, light wind. The desk is staffed; the Director of Flight Operations, the ASO and the General Manager are on call.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states who is on duty, where the fleet register and the 0800 log are, and how Harwick Police would reach the Group.

msel.event: System Log: Harwick Police’s detection vendor console, shared with the Group’s liaison: a small quadcopter broadcasting standard Remote ID, serial 1F7Q-ZX43-0915, has circled the fairgrounds crowd at about 240 ft AGL since 11:01. The broadcast operator position is in the fairgrounds north lot, next to the Group’s perimeter fence. The sergeant at the command post asks whether any Group aircraft is airborne.
msel.expectedAction: The liaison passes the request to the flight operations desk at once; the Director of Flight Operations answers within five minutes from the schedule and the fleet register (HUOG-ERP 8.4); no Group aircraft is launched to look.

metrics.name: Proving the Fleet Was Grounded
metrics.fail: The Group answered Harwick Police late or from memory, or launched an aircraft to look.
metrics.pass: The desk answered within five minutes from the register and the 0800 log (I-02), the serial was compared (I-04) and Hangar 1 was counted and photographed (I-09).
metrics.excellence: The answer to police carried times and evidence, and the photographs reached the command post before the press asked.

metrics.name: Supporting Police Without Interfering
metrics.fail: Group staff approached the operator, the drone or the evidence, or tried to follow it.
metrics.pass: An RPIC went to the command post with a clear brief (I-03); gate access was answered at I-08; staff stayed away at I-10 and I-12; records were copied for police at I-17.
metrics.excellence: The gate code was changed at I-12 and the RPIC’s notes were preserved for the record.

metrics.name: The Public Statement Decision
metrics.fail: The Group kept repeating “no Group aircraft were flying” after I-12 without saying who the operator was, or named him to the press.
metrics.pass: At I-14 the General Manager decided what to say with Corporate Communications and the ASO, consistent with the police statement, and recorded the basis; the crew member was taken off flight duties pending review (I-15).
metrics.excellence: The Group spoke before or with the police, without naming him, and gave CP&L (I-18) and the press (I-19) the same facts.

metrics.name: Records and Regulator
metrics.fail: The FSDO heard nothing from the Group, or heard speculation about the employee.
metrics.pass: The ASO answered the FSDO with facts (I-13) and drafted the event record and follow-up (I-20).
metrics.excellence: The team agreed an interim rule on personal flights near Group sites and fair-week gate codes at I-20.

hotwash.methodDescription: Each team names three things that went well and three that did not; the facilitator writes them up and looks for the same issue in more than one team.

questions.text: How long did it take to tell Harwick Police that every Group aircraft was grounded, and what evidence backed it?
Was “no Group aircraft were flying” still the right public line once the operator was found? What did you decide to say, and why?
Did anyone want to launch, follow or approach the drone or its operator? What stopped them?
What should the Group’s rule be on staff flying their own drones near Horton Field and during public events?
What did CP&L hear, from whom, and before or after the news?

simcellScripts.trigger: The Group calls the command post, or the liaison is asked for anything.
hardQuestions: Is it yours? I need a yes or no with a time on it.
Who can open the gate on your perimeter road?
Can your pilot tell me whether that Remote ID is real or spoofed?
concessions: Accepts the 0800 count and the register as proof the fleet is grounded.
Keeps the drone and controller as evidence; asks only for copies of Group records.

simcellScripts.trigger: The ASO calls, or no one has by 13:10.
hardQuestions: Was this a Group operation? How do you know?
What is your policy on employees flying their own aircraft near your sites?
concessions: Accepts a written follow-up with the records; does not tell the Group what to do with the employee.

hardQuestions: I was off duty with my own drone. Why is this the company’s business?
